cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), and it's called a Maskil. Most songs open with a love story, but David opens by telling us who's blessed.

cards.question: David's first blessing goes to the person who has never sinned.

cards.text: Then David says it a second way: blessed is the man whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him. That's the bill showing up stamped PAID IN FULL, and you never sent a dime!

cards.question: David adds one more thing about this blessed man. Besides being forgiven, what's true of him?

answers.text: There is no deceit in his spirit
There is no fear in his heart
There is no pride in his eyes

cards.text: Now David gets personal and tells about a time he kept silent. Friend, that's putting tape over the check engine light and hoping the engine forgets.

cards.question: While David kept silent, what happened to his body?

answers.text: His bones became brittle from groaning
His knees grew weak from fasting
His eyes grew dim from weeping

cards.text: And it wasn't only his bones. Day and night, David tells the LORD, Your hand was heavy on me.

cards.question: With the LORD's hand heavy on him, David says his strength was drained as in the winter cold.
Then something changed. David turned to the LORD and did not ___ his iniquity.
David says he will confess his transgressions to the LORD. What does the LORD do?

answers.text: He forgives the guilt of his sin
He lays a penalty upon him
He turns His face from him

cards.text: Look at the order: David says he'll confess, and the very next words are "and You forgave the guilt of my sin." No waiting room, no take-a-number, faster than my oven preheats!
David's told his own story, and now he says what it means for all the godly. He's that guy who taped over his check engine light, now telling EVERYBODY at work to go get theirs looked at!

cards.question: After what David went through, what does he want all the godly to do?

answers.text: Pray to the LORD while He may be found
Wait on the LORD until the storm has passed
Keep silent before the LORD in their trouble

cards.question: David pictures great waters rising, and he says they will not come near.

cards.text: Then David tells the LORD, "You are my hiding place." He quit hiding his iniquity and started hiding IN God, and friend, that beats the back of a junk drawer by a MILE!

cards.question: The LORD protects David from trouble and surrounds him with songs of ___.

cards.text: Then the psalm makes a promise: "I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will give you counsel and watch over you." That's not just directions, friend, that's directions with somebody riding shotgun the WHOLE trip!

cards.question: Right after that promise comes a warning: don't be like the horse or mule, which have no ___.

cards.text: They have to be controlled with bit and bridle just to make them come. Friend, that's me at a group photo. Somebody's gotta drag me in by the apron strings!
Then the psalm sets two kinds of people side by side: the wicked, and the one who trusts in the LORD. I'm leaning in with my eyebrows up like a judge on a baking show, friend.

cards.question: The psalm says the wicked have only a few sorrows.
And the one who trusts in the LORD? What surrounds him?

cards.text: Last line, friend. David has a word for the righteous ones, the upright in heart, and I'm already dabbing my eyes with my mustache before he even says it.

cards.question: How does David call the righteous to respond to the LORD?

answers.text: Be glad and shout for joy
